summary: Parses heterogeneous agent run artifacts into a structured hierarchical trace tree, localizes the earliest failure stage, and replays diagnostic signals to recover failed runs under matched budgets.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — directly maps to the AIBlocked → RESET_TO_TODO gap; checkpoint-based plan repair builds on this failure-localization pattern

source: Memanto: Typed Semantic Memory with Information-Theoretic Retrieval for Long-Horizon Agents
summary: Universal memory layer with 13 typed memory categories and a no-indexing semantic search engine delivering sub-90ms retrieval; achieves 89.8% on LongMemEval, beating all graph/vector systems with a single query.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — directly addresses the no-cross-run-memory limitation; episodic run memory issue built on this architecture

summary: Production analysis showing 85% cost savings at 95% quality parity by routing tasks to cheap models and reserving frontier models for the complex 20%; RouteLLM peer-reviewed backing.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — AgentForge has hardcoded agent-to-model mapping; Run schema already has plannerRuntime/executorRuntime fields ready for dynamic population

source: Escher-Loop: Mutual Evolution by Closed-Loop Self-Referential Optimization
summary: Maintains two coevolving populations — task agents and optimizer agents — where optimizer scores are updated from task agent wins/losses, achieving superior peak scores on math optimization problems.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — targets open-ended optimization problems; AgentForge's deterministic state machine and CLI subprocess model don't support the continuous coevolution loop this requires

source: PASTE / B-PASTE: Pattern-Aware Speculative Tool Execution
summary: Predicts and pre-executes likely future tool calls during LLM thinking time, reducing task completion time 43.5% and tool latency 1.8x by exploiting stable agent-level control flow patterns.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — PASTE targets API-based tool-calling latency; AgentForge's bottleneck is CLI subprocess duration, not tool-call prediction. The model doesn't apply cleanly to subprocess-spawning agents.

summary: Three-tier memory model: core (always in-context), archival (vector store), recall (conversation history); agents explicitly call memory management functions to move information between tiers.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — the tiered model is relevant to future episodic memory work but the Memanto paper supersedes it for the immediate issue; Letta requires agent-side function calling not available in CLI subprocess model

source: LangGraph 1.2.0 — DeltaChannel and v3 Streaming API
summary: Adds type-safe streaming (v2/v3 content-block-centric API), DeltaChannel (incremental-delta checkpointing instead of full re-serialization), and finer-grained node timeout/error-recovery controls.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — LangGraph streaming innovations don't map to AgentForge's CLI subprocess model where output is captured at process close, not streamed through a graph node API

source: Glean Trace Learning: Offline Teacher/Student Run Comparison
summary: Compares strong 'teacher' and constrained 'student' runs to distill reliable strategies into compact memories; retrieved at runtime to improve correctness and efficiency without fine-tuning.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — key inspiration for HID-159 repair context and HID-161 episodic memory; the offline distillation pattern fits AgentForge's artifact model well

source: OpenTelemetry GenAI Semantic Conventions for Agent Telemetry
summary: Emerging standard for agent telemetry — typed spans for tool calls, agent steps, and LLM invocations with MCP tracing layer; becoming the common language for cross-framework observability.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — would provide a standards-compliant telemetry layer for ProcessRunner metrics, but spec is still evolving and not yet stable enough to standardize on

source: ZenBrain: Neuroscience-Inspired 7-Layer Memory Architecture for Autonomous AI
summary: Proposes a 7-layer hierarchical memory inspired by human neuroscience (sensory, working, episodic, semantic, procedural, prospective, metacognitive); demonstrated on simulated autonomous tasks.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — research-stage architecture too complex for near-term implementation; AgentForge needs practical episodic memory, not full cognitive architecture emulation

source: Cost-Aware Speculative Execution for LLM-Agent Workflows
summary: Five-dimension cost model for speculative agent execution factoring token cost, latency, rollback overhead, speculation accuracy, and resource contention; integrated scheduling algorithm.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — requires parallel branch execution infrastructure that AgentForge currently lacks; appropriate as a follow-on after parallel execution support is added

source: ICLR 2026 Workshop on AI with Recursive Self-Improvement
summary: Workshop proceedings covering self-rewriting codebases, continual fine-tuning pipelines, and adversarial co-evolution; consensus finding is that self-improvement only works in verifiable domains.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — theoretical framework; useful background but not directly actionable as a specific feature for AgentForge's explicit-state-machine model

source: Karpathy AutoResearch: Automated ML Experiment Loop
summary: 630-line open-source tool that runs ML experiments in a loop under a fixed compute budget, keeping only changes that beat the current best; 21k GitHub stars in days of release.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — targets ML experiment optimization, not software engineering task orchestration; the eval-loop pattern is interesting but out of scope for AgentForge's Linear issue → code flow
